messages:
Nate (Support): FYI - Acme reported a bunch of 500s from /v1/rerank when their batch contains emoji-heavy titles and some control bytes. Ticket INC-2026 opened by Jorge.
Jorge (Acme): Repro steps: POST /v1/rerank with 50 items, two items have emojis and one item had a truncated blob from upstream. Sometimes response is 500, sometimes scores are all -inf.
Nate (Support): Logged the raw payload from their retry (sanitized):
```json
{
  "query": "best restaurants",
  "candidates": ["Sushi \ud83c\udf63", "Cafe\u0000 downtown", "Taco place"]
}
```
Nate (Support): Error from runtime: `internal error: invalid UTF-8 sequence at offset 72`
Priya (oncall): @tom can you take a look at runtime logs for that ts? I'm seeing a spike in 5xxs from rerank around 1912349900-1912350200. :eyes:
Tom (eng-runtime): Jumping in. I pulled service logs for that window — we get a UTF-8 decode failure in the request parsing layer before it hits model. Stack excerpt: `payload_parser.cpp:87: decode_utf8: Assertion 'is_valid' failed` then a SIG 500 handler. Looks like the parser chokes on embedded NUL and some ill-formed surrogate pairs.
Maya (eng-ml): Surrogate pairs + embedded NULs can break our candidate tokenization path. If the tokenization step receives invalid byte sequences, the KV cache path can return NaN scores which downstream get turned into -inf in the ranking aggregator.
Nate (Support): Customer says they get intermittent failures depending on which upstream job produced the string. They asked for a quick workaround they can apply on their side.
Tom (eng-runtime): Short-term workaround: sanitize inputs before sending: remove `\u0000`, normalize to NFC, and replace invalid UTF-8 with the U+FFFD replacement char. Example snippet we recommended: `candidates = [s.replace('\u0000','') for s in candidates]` and then `s.encode('utf-8',errors='replace').decode('utf-8')` to strip bad bytes.
Jorge (Acme): Ok we'll try a pre-send sanitizer. Any config we can toggle on our account to avoid this server-side?
Priya (oncall): No existing toggle. We should not silently accept invalid encodings at the edge without logging — but we can return a 400 with a clear message instead of 500. That will help customers fix inputs.
Maya (eng-ml): Agreed. Proposal: add a validation step in the API gateway to detect non-decodable sequences and return `400 Invalid UTF-8 in candidate[<i>]` with a sample snippet. Also for Private deployments, provide an opt-in `allow_malformed_input` that maps invalid bytes to U+FFFD.
Tom (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR to change the parse behavior: 1) validate and 400, 2) if a header `X-Rerank-Allow-Repair: true` is set we'll attempt auto-repair using replacement. Will add structured logs for the offending bytes.
Nate (Support): PR would help. In the meantime Acme will sanitize client-side. Jorge — please paste back if the sanitizer stops the 500s or if you still see -inf scores.
Jorge (Acme): Quick update after client patch: removed NULs and replaced malformed bytes -> no 500s in a 30-min run. Scores look sane now. Thanks.
Maya (eng-ml): For longer-term mitigation: I'll add a unit test in the tokenization harness that feeds surrogate, ZWJ sequences, and embedded NULs and asserts no NaNs propagate. Also add a regression test in the rerank eval suite.
Tom (eng-runtime): Created tracking issue RNW-587, and PR #4021 to add validation + `X-Rerank-Allow-Repair` support. Canarying on staging now.
Priya (oncall): Once canary is green, we can roll to prod behind a feature flag and coordinate with support for impacted customers.
Nate (Support): Noted. I'll update ticket INC-2026: recommended client-side sanitizer + we're deploying a server-side validation/repair option. Will email Jorge when feature flag is live.
Jorge (Acme): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please include the minimal sanitizer snippet we can paste into our worker.
Nate (Support): Pasted snippet (python):
```py
def sanitize_candidate(s):
    s = s.replace('\x00','')
    return s.encode('utf-8',errors='replace').decode('utf-8')
```
Nate (Support): Marking as provisional-resolved while Acme confirms stability. Will reopen if errors return. :white_check_mark:
SupportBot: Incident link created: RNW-587 · encoding validation for rerank (https://redwood/issue/RNW-587)
Tom (eng-runtime): Canary looks good, no parsing failures for malformed inputs (we're returning 400 by default, repair honored with header). Rolling to prod tomorrow 02:00 UTC behind ff `rerank_input_validation`. :shipit: 
Maya (eng-ml): Added regression tests and bumped tokenization lib to v2.3.1 in the branch.
Nate (Support): Closing loop with Acme after 24h. Thanks team!
Jorge (Acme): All green after 24h. No more 500s. Thanks everyone. :tada:
